title: Leeds office
content: Harlow Instruments opened its Leeds office in 2014 as the company's first site outside London. The office occupies two floors of the Calder Building on Wellington Street. It employs 112 people, most of them in hardware testing and customer support. The Leeds site manager is Priya Raman, who joined from the Porto office in 2021. Leeds holds the company's main calibration lab, which is booked through the internal portal at least five working days in advance. The annual travel budget for Leeds staff is £84,000. Visitors must sign in at reception on the ground floor and wear a badge at all times. Parking is limited to 20 spaces, allocated by lottery each quarter.

title: Porto office
content: The Porto office was established in 2017 to support customers in Southern Europe. It sits in a converted warehouse near the Douro riverfront. The office employs 41 people across sales, logistics and software localisation. Its annual travel budget is €52,000, which is set in euros and not converted. The Porto team runs the company's Portuguese and Spanish help desks from 8:00 to 18:00 local time. Unlike Leeds, Porto has no calibration lab, so instruments that need recalibration are shipped to Leeds by courier. The site manager is Tomás Aguiar. A rooftop terrace is available for team events and must be reserved through facilities.

title: Tallinn office
content: Harlow Instruments acquired the embedded-software firm Rakvere Systems in 2019, and with it an office in Tallinn. The Tallinn office opened under the Harlow name in March 2019. It employs 58 people, nearly all of them firmware engineers. Tallinn does not have a customer help desk; its engineers join support calls only when a ticket is escalated to level three. The office has a travel budget of €39,000 per year. Most hardware prototypes are designed in Tallinn and then built and tested in Leeds. Staff in Tallinn work a four-day compressed week from June to August.

title: Travel policy
content: All Harlow Instruments employees must book work travel through the Voyant booking tool. Economy class is required for flights under six hours. Flights of six hours or longer may be booked in premium economy with approval from a site manager. Hotel costs are reimbursed up to £140 per night in the United Kingdom and €150 per night elsewhere in Europe. Meals are covered by a daily allowance of £45, or €50 outside the UK. Rail travel is preferred for any journey under four hours. Receipts must be submitted within 30 days of return. Claims submitted after 60 days are not reimbursed.

title: Equipment loans
content: Employees may borrow test equipment for fieldwork using the loan register. Standard loans last up to 14 days. Oscilloscopes and spectrum analysers are limited to 7 days because demand is high. Each loan must be approved by the borrower's line manager. Equipment that leaves the United Kingdom requires an ATA carnet, which the logistics team in Porto arranges. Damage must be reported within 24 hours using form EQ-7. Late returns are flagged to the site manager after 3 days. The register is audited every quarter.

title: Onboarding
content: New starters at every Harlow site complete a two-week onboarding programme. The first week covers safety training, company systems and an introduction to each product line. In the second week, new staff shadow a colleague in their own team. Firmware engineers also complete a secure coding course, which takes about 12 hours. Every new starter is assigned a buddy from a different team. Laptops are issued on the first morning and must be encrypted before connecting to the network. Probation lasts six months for all roles.

title: Incident MW-2291: Ashby pumping station
content: On 3 February, the Ashby pumping station lost mains power at 04:12 after a substation fault. The backup generator started automatically but shut down 26 minutes later because of a fuel filter blockage. Supply pressure in the Ashby and Coleford districts fell below the statutory minimum for 2 hours and 40 minutes. Around 3,800 households were affected. Bottled water was distributed from the Coleford community hall. The generator's fuel filters are now replaced every 6 months instead of every 12. The incident was closed on 17 February.

title: Incident MW-2304: Breck Lane main burst
content: A 300 mm cast-iron main burst under Breck Lane at 19:50 on 11 February. The road was closed for three days while the pipe was replaced. Approximately 1,150 households lost supply for up to 9 hours. This was the third failure on the same main since 2021. It has now been added to the replacement programme for the next financial year. Crews from the Halden depot carried out the repair. Compensation of £30 was paid automatically to each affected household.

title: Incident MW-2317: Coleford reservoir turbidity
content: Routine sampling at Coleford reservoir on 20 February found turbidity of 4.2 NTU, above the 1.0 NTU treatment limit. The cause was heavy rainfall washing sediment into the inlet channel. The treatment works switched to the Denholm aquifer for 36 hours. No boil-water notice was required because treated water stayed within limits throughout. Inlet screens were cleaned, and a second turbidity sensor was installed upstream. Sampling frequency at Coleford has been raised from weekly to daily until the end of April.

title: Pressure standards
content: Mirefield Water Authority must maintain a minimum supply pressure of 10 metres head at the property boundary. Interruptions longer than 4 hours must be reported to the regulator within one working day. Households without water for more than 12 hours are entitled to £50 compensation, rising by £25 for each further 12 hours. Planned interruptions require 48 hours' notice. Hospitals, care homes and dialysis patients on the priority register are contacted first during any unplanned outage. The register currently lists 612 addresses.

title: Depots
content: The Authority runs three maintenance depots. Halden depot covers the northern districts and has 14 repair crews. Ferris Road depot covers the south with 9 crews. The smallest, Upton Marsh, has 5 crews and handles rural mains and the reservoirs. Each crew consists of two technicians and a supervisor on call. Emergency response targets are one hour in urban districts and two hours in rural ones. Depot vans are fitted with GPS trackers so that control room staff can dispatch the nearest crew.

title: Customer communications
content: During an unplanned outage, the control room posts an update on the service map within 30 minutes. Text alerts are sent to registered customers in affected postcodes. Updates continue every two hours until supply is restored. Once the incident is closed, a summary is published on the incidents page within ten working days. Customers can request a full incident report by email. Complaints about outages are answered within 20 working days.

title: Summer timetable
content: Castellan Rail's summer timetable runs from 1 June to 14 September. On the Marrow Valley line, weekday trains leave Castellan Central every 20 minutes between 06:00 and 20:00. After 20:00 the service drops to one train every 40 minutes. The last departure to Hollin Bridge is at 23:25. Weekend services on the Marrow Valley line run every 30 minutes all day. The coastal line to Saltmere gains two extra evening trains on Fridays. Engineering works close the Saltmere branch on the weekend of 9 and 10 August, when replacement buses run.

title: Fares
content: An anytime single from Castellan Central to Hollin Bridge costs £7.80. An off-peak single on the same route costs £5.20 and is valid after 09:30 on weekdays. The anytime single to Saltmere costs £11.40. Day returns are priced at 1.5 times the single fare. Children aged 5 to 15 pay half fare, and children under 5 travel free. Fares rise by an average of 3.1% each January. Tickets bought on board without a valid reason incur a penalty fare of £20 or twice the full single fare, whichever is greater.

title: Railcards
content: The Valley Railcard costs £30 a year and gives one third off off-peak fares. It is available to anyone who lives in the Marrow Valley postcode area. The Coastal Saver card costs £45 a year and gives 25% off all fares to Saltmere. Neither card can be used for season tickets. Railcards are issued digitally through the Castellan app. A photocard is required for holders aged 16 to 25. Lost digital railcards can be restored free of charge once a year.

title: Accessibility
content: Every station on the Marrow Valley line has step-free access except Kessock, where the footbridge is the only route between platforms. A lift at Kessock is scheduled to open in March next year. Passengers who need assistance can book it up to two hours before travel through the Passenger Assist service. Staffed stations provide ramps for boarding. At unstaffed stations, the train guard deploys the ramp. Assistance dogs travel free on all services. Wheelchair spaces can be reserved on the coastal line but not on the Marrow Valley line.

title: Delay Repay
content: Passengers delayed by 15 minutes or more can claim compensation under Delay Repay. A delay of 15 to 29 minutes earns 25% of the single fare. A delay of 30 to 59 minutes earns 50%. Delays of an hour or more earn a full refund of the single fare. Claims must be made within 28 days of travel. Compensation is paid to the original payment card or as rail vouchers. Season ticket holders claim based on the daily cost of their ticket.

title: Bikes and luggage
content: Folding bicycles can be carried on any service. Non-folding bicycles are allowed on Marrow Valley trains outside the peak hours of 07:00 to 09:30 and 16:30 to 18:30. Each train has space for four bicycles, which cannot be reserved. On the coastal line, bicycle spaces must be reserved at least an hour in advance. Each passenger may bring two large suitcases and one small bag. Surfboards are permitted on the coastal line only. E-scooters are banned on all trains and at all stations.

title: Trial OB-114: velastrin
content: Trial OB-114 tested velastrin, an oral treatment for chronic migraine, in 420 adults across 18 clinics. Participants took either 25 mg of velastrin or a placebo once a day for 12 weeks. Monthly migraine days fell by 4.1 on velastrin compared with 1.9 on placebo. The most common side effect was mild nausea, reported by 11% of participants on the drug. Seven participants left the trial because of side effects. Results were presented at the Lisbon neurology congress in May.

title: Trial OB-127: corvanide
content: Trial OB-127 evaluated corvanide for high blood pressure that had not responded to two other medicines. It enrolled 260 patients at 9 hospitals. Patients received 10 mg of corvanide daily for 24 weeks. Systolic blood pressure fell by an average of 14 mmHg, against 5 mmHg in the placebo group. This effect appeared within the first four weeks and was maintained to the end of the study. Dizziness was reported by 6% of patients. The trial was paused for a month in 2024 while a labelling error on the placebo packs was corrected.

title: Trial OB-131: velastrin in adolescents
content: Trial OB-131 is testing velastrin in adolescents aged 12 to 17. The dose is 10 mg, lower than the adult dose, because of differences in body weight. Recruitment began in January and has reached 96 of a planned 150 participants. An independent safety board reviews the data every three months. No serious adverse events have been reported so far. Results are expected in the second half of next year.

title: Manufacturing
content: Velastrin tablets are manufactured at Orrin's plant in Galway, which produced 38 million tablets last year. Corvanide is made under contract by Helder Pharma in Rotterdam. The Galway plant passed its most recent regulatory inspection in October with no major findings. A second production line for velastrin will open in Galway next spring, doubling capacity. Active ingredients for both medicines are sourced from two suppliers each, so that no product depends on a single source.

title: Development pipeline
content: Orrin Biotech has five medicines in development. Two are in phase III: velastrin for chronic migraine and corvanide for resistant hypertension. Ostrelin, a treatment for nerve pain, is in phase II. The remaining two are in preclinical development and have not been named. Orrin expects to file for approval of velastrin in the European Union first, followed by the United Kingdom six months later. The company does not plan to seek approval in the United States until a second phase III trial is complete.

title: Participant support
content: Participants in Orrin trials are reimbursed for travel to clinic visits up to £60 per visit. Parking at partner hospitals is free for participants. A nurse helpline is open from 08:00 to 20:00 every day. Participants can leave a trial at any time without giving a reason, and their care will not be affected. After a trial ends, participants who benefited may continue treatment through an extension study. Summaries of results are sent to all participants in plain language.

title: Credit requirements
content: Undergraduate students at Brightwater University must pass 360 credits to graduate with an honours degree. Each year of full-time study carries 120 credits. A standard module is worth 15 credits, and a dissertation is worth 40. Students may carry up to 20 failed credits into the next year, provided they pass them by the end of that year. Students who fail more than 20 credits must repeat the failed modules before progressing. Part-time students take between 45 and 90 credits a year.

title: Coursework deadlines
content: Coursework must be submitted through the Orbit portal by 14:00 on the deadline day. Work submitted up to 24 hours late receives a penalty of 10 percentage points. Work submitted between 24 hours and 5 days late is capped at the pass mark of 40%. Anything later than 5 days receives a mark of zero. Students with an approved extension are exempt from these penalties. Extensions of up to 7 days can be granted by the module leader.

title: Mitigating circumstances
content: Requests for extensions longer than 7 days go to the Mitigating Circumstances Panel. The panel meets every two weeks during term. It can grant extensions of up to 28 days or allow a student to sit an assessment at the next opportunity as if for the first time. Supporting evidence, such as a medical note, must be provided within 10 working days of the request. Self-certification is accepted for absences of up to 5 days, twice per academic year.

title: Degree classification
content: The final degree classification is based on second-year and final-year marks. Second-year modules count for 30% and final-year modules for 70%. A weighted average of 70 or above earns a first-class degree. An average from 60 to 69 earns an upper second, and 50 to 59 a lower second. A third-class degree is awarded for averages between 40 and 49. Students within 2 marks of a boundary are considered for the higher class if more than half of their final-year credits are in the higher band.

title: Library and study spaces
content: The Hartley Library is open 24 hours a day during exam periods and from 08:00 to midnight at other times. Students may borrow up to 25 items at once. Standard loans last three weeks and renew automatically unless another reader requests the item. The Mercer Study Hub has 140 bookable desks, which can be reserved for up to four hours. It closes at 22:00 every day, including during exams. Group study rooms in the Hartley Library can be booked for a maximum of two hours.

title: Placements
content: Students on four-year sandwich degrees spend their third year on a professional placement. The placement year carries 120 credits but does not count towards the degree classification. Students must secure a placement by 30 June at the end of their second year. Those who do not find one transfer automatically to the three-year version of their degree. Placement students pay a reduced tuition fee of £1,850 for that year. A visiting tutor meets each student twice during the placement.

title: Postmortem KC-5512: eu-north storage
content: On 8 April, object storage in the eu-north region returned errors for 47 minutes, starting at 13:05 UTC. A configuration change intended for a test cluster was applied to production. About 18% of read requests in the region failed during the incident. The change was rolled back at 13:38, but caches took a further 14 minutes to recover. Kestrel Cloud now requires a second engineer to approve any change that targets a production cluster. Affected customers received a 10% service credit for April.

title: Postmortem KC-5530: us-east DNS
content: Internal DNS in the us-east region failed for 22 minutes on 15 April. The cause was an expired signing certificate on two resolver nodes. Virtual machines could not resolve service names, so many customer applications timed out. The certificate had been renewed in the certificate store but not deployed to those nodes. It is now deployed automatically by the fleet manager. Certificate expiry alerts have been moved from 7 days to 30 days before expiry. No service credit was issued because the monthly uptime target was still met.

title: Postmortem KC-5561: ap-south load balancers
content: Load balancers in ap-south dropped roughly 3% of new connections for 3 hours and 10 minutes on 29 April. A software upgrade introduced a memory leak that caused nodes to restart under high traffic. The upgrade had passed testing because test traffic was below the level that triggered the leak. The fleet was rolled back to the previous version. Load tests now replay recorded production traffic at 150% of peak. Customers in ap-south received a 25% service credit for April.

title: Service credits
content: Kestrel Cloud's uptime target is 99.95% per calendar month for each regional service. If monthly uptime falls below 99.95% but stays at or above 99.0%, customers receive a 10% credit. Between 95.0% and 99.0%, the credit is 25%. Below 95.0%, customers receive a 100% credit for that service. Credits must be claimed within 60 days of the end of the month. They are applied to the next invoice and cannot be exchanged for cash.

title: Change management
content: All production changes at Kestrel Cloud are scheduled through the Beacon change calendar. Standard changes can be deployed at any time if they have an approved template. Normal changes require approval from a second engineer and must avoid the peak hours of the target region. Emergency changes may skip the calendar but must be reviewed within 48 hours. Changes are frozen for all regions during the last week of December. Each region has a rollback plan that must be tested every quarter.

title: On-call
content: Each regional team keeps two engineers on call at all times: a primary and a secondary. The primary must acknowledge a page within 5 minutes. If they do not, the secondary is paged automatically. On-call shifts last one week and rotate on Mondays at 10:00 local time. Engineers are paid an allowance of £180 per week on call, plus overtime for incidents outside working hours. No engineer may be on call for more than two weeks in any six-week period.

title: Branch opening hours
content: Vallin County Library has six branches. The Central branch in Market Square is open from 09:00 to 20:00 Monday to Saturday and from 11:00 to 16:00 on Sunday. The Eastgate and Riverside branches open from 09:30 to 17:30 Monday to Saturday. Neither of them opens on Sunday. Thornby branch opens on Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday mornings only. The mobile library visits 23 villages on a fortnightly route.

title: Membership and fines
content: Library membership is free for anyone who lives, works or studies in Vallin County. Adults can borrow up to 15 items at a time, and children up to 10. Books are lent for three weeks and DVDs for one week. Overdue adult books are charged at 25p per day, up to a maximum of £6 per item. Children's items are never fined. Members who owe more than £10 cannot borrow until the balance is paid.

title: Riverside refurbishment
content: The Riverside branch will close for refurbishment from 4 November to 20 January. During the closure, a temporary service will run from the Riverside Community Centre on Tuesdays and Fridays. Items on loan from Riverside can be returned to any other branch. The refurbishment will add a children's area, 12 new public computers and step-free access to the first floor. It is funded by a £420,000 grant from the county council. The branch's local history collection will move to Central permanently.

title: Events
content: Storytime for children under five runs at Central every Wednesday at 10:30 and at Eastgate every Friday at 10:00. The Vallin Reading Group meets on the first Monday of each month at Central. Its members choose the next book by vote. Free digital skills sessions for adults run at Eastgate on Tuesday afternoons. Places are limited to eight people and must be booked by phone. The summer reading challenge for children aged 4 to 11 runs from July to early September.

title: Digital services
content: Members can borrow e-books and audiobooks through the Libby app using their card number and PIN. Up to 8 digital titles can be borrowed at once. Digital loans return automatically after 14 days, so there are never fines on them. The library also offers free access to an online newspaper archive dating back to 1851. Public computers can be used for up to two hours a day. Printing costs 10p per black-and-white page and 50p per colour page.

title: Room hire
content: Meeting rooms at Central and Eastgate can be hired by community groups. The large room at Central holds 60 people and costs £25 per hour. The Eastgate room holds 20 people and costs £12 per hour. Registered charities receive a 50% discount. Rooms must be booked at least five working days in advance. Bookings can be cancelled free of charge up to 48 hours before the start time.

title: Patch 3.4.0
content: Patch 3.4.0 for Ironvale launched on 12 March. It raised the level cap from 60 to 65 and added the Sunken Archive dungeon. The Sunken Archive is designed for five players and has four bosses. Crafting materials from the new dungeon cannot be traded. The patch also reduced the cooldown of the Warden's Shield Wall ability from 120 seconds to 90 seconds. Matchmaking for ranked arenas now considers the last 20 matches instead of the last 10.

title: Patch 3.4.1
content: Patch 3.4.1 was a hotfix released on 15 March. It fixed a crash that occurred when more than 40 players entered the Sunken Archive entrance at the same time. The final boss of the Sunken Archive, the Drowned Scholar, had its health reduced by 8%. This change applies to normal difficulty only. The patch also corrected a bug that let players skip the dungeon's second boss. Players who had skipped that boss did not lose their rewards.

title: Patch 3.5.0
content: Patch 3.5.0 arrived on 23 April with the new Tidebreaker class. The Tidebreaker uses a two-handed trident and can switch between two stances. Every account received one free character slot to try the class. The patch added cross-server trading for all tradeable items. It also increased the maximum guild size from 150 to 200 members. The Warden's Shield Wall cooldown was raised again, to 105 seconds, after feedback that the class was too strong in arenas.

title: Festival of Tides
content: The Festival of Tides runs from 1 June to 30 June. During the event, players earn Tide Tokens by completing daily quests. The event shop sells a mount for 900 tokens and a cosmetic cloak for 400 tokens. Tokens that are not spent by 7 July are converted to gold at a rate of 5 gold per token. Event quests are available to characters of level 20 and above. The event returns every year with new rewards.

title: Server maintenance
content: Scheduled maintenance takes place every Tuesday from 06:00 to 09:00 UTC. During maintenance, all game servers are offline, but the forums stay available. Extended maintenance before a major patch can last up to 6 hours and is announced a week in advance. Players who are logged in when maintenance starts are disconnected after a 15-minute warning. Maintenance compensation of 200 gold is granted when maintenance overruns by more than an hour.

title: Account security
content: Tessaract Games recommends that every player enable two-factor authentication. Accounts with two-factor authentication receive an exclusive in-game pet. Support staff will never ask for a password. Stolen accounts can be restored to their state from up to 14 days before the theft. Items traded away by an attacker are returned if the trade happened within that period. Accounts that are shared or sold are suspended for 30 days on a first offence.

title: Membership
content: Norhaven Housing Co-operative has 84 homes across three buildings: Alder House, Birch Court and Cedar Row. Every tenant over 18 becomes a member with one vote. Members are expected to contribute at least four hours of volunteer work each month. The general meeting is held on the second Thursday of every quarter. A quorum requires 25 members to be present. New members attend an induction session within their first month.

title: Rent and charges
content: Monthly rent is £640 for a one-bedroom flat, £790 for two bedrooms and £925 for three bedrooms. A service charge of £38 per month covers cleaning, lighting and garden upkeep in shared areas. Rents are reviewed each April and have not risen by more than inflation since 2016. Rent is due on the first working day of the month. Members who fall more than two months behind must agree a repayment plan with the finance committee.

title: Deposits and moving in
content: A deposit equal to one month's rent is required before moving in. It is held in a government-approved protection scheme. Keys are issued once the tenancy agreement is signed and the first month's rent has been paid. Each home is inspected with the new member on moving day, and photographs are added to the inventory. Members moving from another co-operative can transfer their deposit if the other co-op agrees.

title: Repairs
content: Emergency repairs, such as a burst pipe or a total loss of heating, are attended within 4 hours. Urgent repairs, including a broken lock or a leaking roof, are attended within 3 working days. Routine repairs are completed within 28 days. Repairs are reported through the members' portal or by phone to the maintenance coordinator, Dafydd Price. Members must allow access for repairs with 24 hours' notice, except in emergencies.

title: Pets and gardens
content: Cats and small caged animals are allowed in all homes. Dogs are permitted in Cedar Row only, because it is the only building with private gardens. No more than two pets may be kept in any home. The shared garden behind Alder House has 16 allotment beds, allocated each February by ballot. Beds that are not used for a whole season are reallocated. Barbecues are allowed in the shared garden on weekends until 21:00.

title: Leaving the co-op
content: Members who wish to leave must give two months' written notice. The home is inspected before the member moves out. Deposits are returned within 20 days of the tenancy ending, minus any agreed deductions for damage or unpaid rent. Departing members lose their vote from the day their tenancy ends. Anyone who leaves can apply to rejoin, but they join the waiting list, which currently has 210 households.

title: Stages
content: Pellmoor Festival takes place from 14 to 16 August on Hawes Common. There are four stages: the Main Stage, the Orchard Tent, the Lantern Stage and the Brook Arena. The Main Stage closes each night at 23:00 because of the noise licence. The Orchard Tent hosts acoustic acts and has room for 2,500 people. The Lantern Stage programmes electronic music until 01:00. It is the only stage open after midnight.

title: Tickets
content: A weekend ticket costs £165 and includes camping. Day tickets cost £70 for Friday and £85 for Saturday or Sunday. Children under 12 enter free with a paying adult, and teenagers aged 12 to 17 pay half price. Tickets are sold only through the official website and cannot be resold except through its exchange service. Each buyer may purchase up to six tickets. Wristbands are posted two weeks before the festival.

title: Camping
content: The general campsite opens at 10:00 on Thursday, the day before the music starts. Campervans must park in the Birchfield field, which requires a £40 permit. Quiet camping is available in the Meadow area for families and anyone who wants to sleep before midnight. Glass bottles are banned from all campsites. Gas stoves are allowed, but open fires are not. The campsites close at 12:00 on the Monday after the festival.

title: Getting there
content: Shuttle buses run from Pellmoor railway station to the festival gate every 15 minutes. A return shuttle ticket costs £8 when bought in advance or £12 on the day. The station is 6 miles from Hawes Common. Car parking costs £20 for the weekend and must be booked in advance. Cycle parking at the main gate is free and supervised during opening hours. Taxis can only drop off and pick up at the Western Lane rank.

title: Accessibility
content: Accessible viewing platforms are provided at the Main Stage and the Brook Arena. The Orchard Tent has level access but no raised platform. Personal assistants of disabled ticket holders receive a free ticket, which must be requested by 1 July. An accessible campsite with powered charging points is located next to the medical tent. Sign-language interpreters are booked for all Main Stage headline sets.

title: Food and sustainability
content: More than 60 food traders operate across the site. Every trader must offer at least one vegetarian option, and half of them are fully vegan. Single-use plastic cups are not sold anywhere at the festival. Drinks are served in reusable cups, which carry a £2 deposit returned at any bar. Water refill points are free. Last year the festival recycled 71% of its waste, and it aims for 80% this year.

title: How it works
content: Dunmore Cycle Hire has 1,400 bikes at 210 docking stations across the city. Bikes are unlocked with the Dunmore Ride app or a contactless bank card at the docking post. Each journey must end at a docking station; bikes left elsewhere incur a £25 recovery fee. The scheme operates 24 hours a day, all year round. About a third of the fleet are electric bikes, marked with a green frame.

title: Prices
content: A single ride on a standard bike costs £1.50 for the first 30 minutes. Each extra 30 minutes costs another £1.50. Electric bikes cost £3.00 for the first 30 minutes and £2.00 for each extra 30 minutes. A monthly pass costs £18 and includes unlimited 45-minute rides on standard bikes. The annual pass costs £120. Students with a valid university card get 30% off both passes.

title: Electric bikes
content: Electric bikes have a top assisted speed of 15.5 mph. The battery gives a range of about 40 miles on a full charge. It is swapped by the operations team when it falls below 20%. Riders can see each bike's battery level in the app before unlocking it. Electric bikes are not available to riders under 18. They must be returned to a station with a charging dock, marked with a lightning symbol.

title: Safety rules
content: Riders must be at least 14 years old to use a standard bike. Helmets are recommended but not required by law. Riding on pavements is prohibited except where signs show a shared path. Every bike has front and rear lights that switch on automatically. Riders must not carry passengers or use a phone while riding. Accounts are suspended for 14 days after three reports of dangerous riding.

title: Faults and support
content: If a bike is faulty, riders should dock it and press the red button on the docking post for 3 seconds. This marks the bike for repair and prevents anyone else from taking it. Riders who report a fault within 10 minutes of unlocking are not charged for that ride. The support line is open from 07:00 to 22:00. Outside those hours, riders can report problems through the app, and they receive a reply the next morning.

title: Station expansion
content: Dunmore City Council approved 35 new docking stations in the eastern districts last autumn. They will be installed in two phases. The first 20 stations are due to open in May, mostly around the new tram stops. The remaining 15 will open in the autumn once road works on Carrick Street are finished. The expansion is paid for by a £2.1 million transport grant and will add 250 bikes to the fleet.

title: Cardiology clinic
content: The cardiology outpatient clinic at Quarry Ridge Hospital runs on Monday, Wednesday and Friday. New patients are seen in the morning session, which starts at 08:30. The current waiting time for a first appointment is 11 weeks. Patients referred as urgent are seen within 14 days. The clinic is on level 2 of the Brackley Wing, next to the imaging department. An echocardiogram is usually booked for the same visit.

title: Dermatology clinic
content: Dermatology clinics are held every weekday in the Harrow Suite on the ground floor. The waiting time for a routine first appointment is 19 weeks. Suspected skin cancer referrals follow a separate pathway. They are seen within two weeks of the referral being received. Photographs of skin lesions can be uploaded through the patient portal before the appointment. The clinic does not treat cosmetic conditions.

title: Physiotherapy
content: Physiotherapy is available to patients referred by a hospital consultant or a GP. Self-referral is accepted for back and neck pain only. The service offers up to six sessions per referral. Each session lasts 40 minutes. Patients who miss two sessions without notice are discharged back to their GP. Hydrotherapy takes place in the pool at the Linden Centre, which is heated to 34 degrees.

title: Parking and transport
content: Visitor parking at Quarry Ridge costs £2.50 for the first hour and £1.50 for each additional hour. Blue badge holders park free in any marked disabled bay. Patients attending for daily treatment, such as dialysis, can apply for a free parking permit. The permit is valid for 3 months and can be renewed at the main reception. A free shuttle bus runs between the Brackley Wing and the Linden Centre every 20 minutes.

title: Appointments and cancellations
content: Appointment letters are sent at least 21 days before the appointment date. Patients can change an appointment once through the booking line without going back to the end of the waiting list. A second change resets the waiting time. Cancellations made less than 24 hours before an appointment are recorded as missed. Text reminders are sent 5 days and 1 day before each appointment.

title: Interpreting service
content: Quarry Ridge provides interpreters free of charge for patients who need them. Face-to-face interpreters must be booked at least 48 hours in advance. Telephone interpreting is available immediately in more than 200 languages. British Sign Language interpreters are booked through the Deaf Access team. Family members are not used as interpreters for clinical conversations, except in an emergency.

title: Aria hatchback
content: The Selwyn Aria is a compact electric hatchback. Its 52 kWh battery gives an official range of 238 miles. The Aria can charge from 10% to 80% in 31 minutes on a rapid charger. It seats five adults and has a boot capacity of 380 litres. Prices start at £27,400 for the Core trim.

title: Vista SUV
content: The Selwyn Vista is a seven-seat electric SUV. It uses a 91 kWh battery with an official range of 312 miles. Rapid charging from 10% to 80% takes 38 minutes. The Vista can tow up to 1,600 kg, the highest figure in the Selwyn range. This makes it popular with caravan owners. The third row of seats folds flat into the floor.

title: Tempo van
content: The Selwyn Tempo is a medium electric van for business customers. Its load area holds 5.8 cubic metres, and its payload is 1,050 kg. The official range is 205 miles. The Tempo is not available to private buyers; it is sold only through Selwyn Business dealers. A refrigerated version will be added next year.

title: Warranty
content: Every new Selwyn car comes with a 4-year or 60,000-mile warranty, whichever comes first. The battery is covered separately for 8 years or 100,000 miles. Selwyn will replace a battery that falls below 70% of its original capacity during that period. Commercial vehicles, including the Tempo, have a 3-year warranty with no mileage limit. Paintwork is covered for 3 years.

title: Servicing
content: Selwyn electric vehicles need a service every 2 years or 20,000 miles. A standard service costs £189 for cars and £245 for vans. Brake fluid is replaced at every second service. Customers can book a mobile technician for minor repairs at home. Servicing at a non-Selwyn garage does not void the warranty if genuine parts are used.

title: Home charging
content: Selwyn offers a 7 kW home charger for £899 including standard installation. It fully charges an Aria in about 8 hours. Installation requires off-street parking and a survey visit. The survey is free and takes around 45 minutes. Customers who buy a new Selwyn car before 31 March receive the charger at half price.

title: Term dates
content: Ashgrove School's autumn term begins on 4 September and ends on 19 December. Half term runs from 27 to 31 October. The spring term starts on 6 January. Staff training days are held on 3 September and 6 January, when pupils do not attend. The summer term ends earlier than usual, on 16 July, because the main hall is being refurbished.

title: Fees
content: Annual tuition fees at Ashgrove are £16,200 for the junior school and £21,900 for the senior school. Fees are payable in three instalments at the start of each term. A sibling discount of 10% applies to the second child and 15% to the third and any further children. Lunches are included in the fees for the junior school. Senior pupils pay £4.20 per lunch through a cashless card.

title: Uniform
content: Senior pupils wear a navy blazer with the school crest, grey trousers or a grey skirt, and a striped tie. Junior pupils wear a green jumper instead of a blazer. The uniform shop in the Weston Building opens on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 15:30 to 17:30. It also sells second-hand items at half the new price. Trainers are not permitted except for PE lessons.

title: Mobile phones
content: Pupils in years 7 to 9 must hand in their phones to their form tutor at registration. They are returned at the end of the school day. Pupils in years 10 and 11 may keep phones switched off in their bags. Sixth-form students may use phones in the common room only. A phone used without permission is confiscated until a parent collects it.

title: Clubs and activities
content: Ashgrove runs more than 40 after-school clubs. Most clubs are free, but the rowing club charges £120 per term to cover coaching and boat hire. The robotics club meets on Wednesdays and has won the regional championship twice. It is open to pupils from year 8 upwards. Clubs finish at 17:00, and a late bus leaves at 17:15.

title: Absence
content: Parents must report an absence by 08:45 on each day their child is away. Holidays during term time are not authorised except in exceptional circumstances. Requests must be made to the head teacher at least four weeks in advance. Pupils with attendance below 90% are referred to the attendance officer. Medical appointments should be booked outside school hours where possible.

title: Routes
content: Merrow Bay Ferries operates three routes from Merrow Harbour. The Kelby route crosses to Kelby Island in 35 minutes. The Strand route to Porthcoll takes 1 hour and 10 minutes. The longest route, to the Farne Rocks nature reserve, takes 2 hours and runs from April to October only. All routes carry foot passengers, but only the Kelby route carries cars.

title: Fares
content: An adult return on the Kelby route costs £14, and a car with driver costs £62 return. The adult return fare to Porthcoll is £22. A return trip to the Farne Rocks costs £38 and includes a guided walk. Children under 16 pay half fare on all routes. Dogs travel free on the Kelby and Strand routes but are not allowed on the Farne Rocks sailing.

title: Timetable
content: In summer, Kelby sailings leave Merrow Harbour every hour from 07:00 to 21:00. In winter the service runs every two hours from 08:00 to 18:00. Porthcoll sailings depart at 09:15, 13:15 and 17:15 all year. The Farne Rocks boat leaves once a day at 10:00. It returns at 16:00 after four hours on the islands.

title: Disruption
content: Sailings may be cancelled when wind speeds exceed 40 knots. Passengers are told of cancellations by text message and on the website. Tickets for cancelled sailings are refunded in full or moved to another sailing free of charge. The Farne Rocks trip is also cancelled if the sea state is too rough to land safely. In that case, passengers can choose a harbour cruise instead.

title: Accessibility
content: The Kelby ferry has a lift between the car deck and the passenger lounge. The smaller Strand ferry has steps to its upper deck, so wheelchair users travel in the lower saloon. The Farne Rocks boat cannot carry wheelchairs because passengers land by small boat. Accessible toilets are available on the Kelby and Strand ferries. Assistance can be booked at the ticket office.

title: Season tickets
content: Island residents can buy a Kelby Resident card for £85 a year. It gives 70% off foot passenger fares on the Kelby route. Commuters to Porthcoll can buy a monthly season ticket for £210. Season tickets cannot be used on the Farne Rocks trip. Lost cards are replaced for a £10 fee.

title: Starter plan
content: Lumen Analytics' Starter plan costs $29 per month. It includes 3 dashboards and data refreshes once a day. Starter accounts can connect up to 2 data sources. API access is not included in the Starter plan. Support is by email only, with replies within two business days.

title: Team plan
content: The Team plan costs $99 per month for up to 10 users. Dashboards are unlimited, and data refreshes every hour. Team accounts can connect up to 15 data sources. API requests are limited to 5,000 per day. Support is available by chat during business hours.

title: Enterprise plan
content: Enterprise pricing is agreed with each customer and starts at $900 per month. It adds single sign-on, audit logs and a dedicated account manager. Data refreshes can run as often as every 5 minutes. The API limit is 100,000 requests per day. It can be raised further on request at no extra cost.

title: Billing
content: All plans can be paid monthly or annually. Annual billing gives two months free. Upgrades take effect immediately and are charged pro rata. Downgrades take effect at the end of the current billing period. Lumen accepts card payments on all plans and bank transfer on Enterprise only.

title: Data retention
content: Raw event data is kept for 90 days on Starter, 13 months on Team and 7 years on Enterprise. Aggregated dashboard data is kept for as long as the account is active. When an account is closed, all data is deleted after 30 days. Customers can export their data at any time as CSV or Parquet files. Deleted dashboards can be restored within 14 days.

title: Security
content: Lumen stores all customer data in data centres in Frankfurt and Dublin. Data is encrypted at rest and in transit. The company completes an independent SOC 2 audit every year. Two-factor authentication is required for all administrator accounts. Customers on the Team and Enterprise plans can restrict access to approved IP address ranges.

title: Glasshouses
content: Fenwick Botanical Gardens has three glasshouses. The Palm House is the largest, rising 18 metres at its central dome. The Arid House holds cacti and succulents from four continents. The Orchid House is kept at 24 degrees and 80% humidity. It is closed on Mondays for maintenance. Photography with tripods is not allowed in any glasshouse.

title: Opening times and admission
content: The gardens open at 10:00 every day except 25 December. They close at 18:00 from April to September and at 16:00 from October to March. Adult admission costs £16.50, and children under 5 enter free. Tickets bought online are 10% cheaper than at the gate. Last entry is one hour before closing.

title: Membership
content: Individual membership costs £68 a year and includes unlimited entry. Joint membership for two adults at the same address costs £115. Members may bring one guest free on up to four visits a year. Members also get 15% off in the garden shop and café. Membership cards are posted within ten days of joining.

title: The Winter Lantern trail
content: The Winter Lantern trail runs on Friday and Saturday evenings from 28 November to 3 January. It follows a 1.5-mile route through the arboretum. Timed tickets cost £21 for adults and £12 for children. The trail is not included in membership. Members can, however, book tickets a week before general sale.

title: Learning programme
content: Fenwick runs free guided tours at 11:00 and 14:00 each weekend. School groups are welcome on weekdays and must book at least three weeks ahead. The herbarium holds more than 250,000 pressed plant specimens. It is open to researchers by appointment only. Adult courses in botanical illustration run over eight weekly sessions.

title: Visitor rules
content: Dogs are welcome in the outdoor gardens if kept on a short lead. They are not allowed in the glasshouses or the café. Cycling is permitted only on the perimeter path. Picnics may be eaten on the Great Lawn. Visitors must not pick flowers, collect seeds or take cuttings from any plant.
